definitions.explanation: The highest grade of shaded Japanese green tea. The tea plants are covered to block sunlight for about three weeks before harvest, which increases the amino acid content and produces a rich, sweet umami flavor with minimal bitterness.

examples.japanese: {玉露|ぎょくろ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{高級|こうきゅう}→高級：08644_koukyuu⟧な⟦{日本茶|にほんちゃ}→日本茶：28691_nihoncha⟧だ。
examples.english: Gyokuro is a high-grade Japanese tea.

examples.japanese: {玉露|ぎょくろ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{低|ひく}い→低い：02947_hikui⟧⟦{温度|おんど}→温度：00333_ondo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦お{湯|ゆ}→お湯：02518_oyu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{淹|い}れる→淹れる：13297_ireru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦コツ→コツ：06658_kotsu⟧だ。
examples.english: The trick to brewing gyokuro is to use low-temperature water.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{歳暮|せいぼ}→お歳暮：06126_oseibo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{宇治|うじ}{産|さん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{玉露|ぎょくろ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{贈|おく}ったら→贈る：09862_okuru⟧、⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧⟦{喜|よろこ}ばれた→喜ぶ：01169_yorokobu⟧。
examples.english: When I gave Uji-grown gyokuro as a year-end gift, it was very well received.

notes:
TEA GRADES:
Japanese green tea grades from highest to lowest:
- {玉露|ぎょくろ}: shade-grown, highest grade
- ⟦{煎茶|せんちゃ}→煎茶：13407_sencha⟧: sun-grown, most common
- ⟦{番茶|ばんちゃ}→番茶：13724_bancha⟧: coarser leaves, everyday tea
- ⟦{抹茶|まっちゃ}→抹茶：10574_maccha⟧: powdered tea (different category)

BREWING NOTE:
{玉露|ぎょくろ} should be brewed at around 50-60°C, much lower than ⟦{煎茶|せんちゃ}→煎茶：13407_sencha⟧ (70-80°C). Using boiling water brings out bitterness and ruins the delicate sweetness.

ETYMOLOGY:
Literally "jade dew" — {玉|ぎょく} (jewel, jade) + {露|ろ} (dew). Named for the pale green color of the brewed tea.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {玉露|ぎょくろ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{淹|い}れる→淹れる：13297_ireru⟧: brew gyokuro
- {宇治|うじ}{玉露|ぎょくろ}: Uji gyokuro (from Kyoto, most prestigious)
- ⟦{高級|こうきゅう}→高級：08644_koukyuu⟧{玉露|ぎょくろ}: premium gyokuro
